metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson a Risky Play in Fantasy Football Right Now
metadata.description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) has struggled to produce at a meaningful level lately, and a lingering ankle injury further complicates his outlook for Week 6 against the New York Jets. Henderson has played fewer than 38% of the snaps in each of the last three weeks, and he has failed to score more than 4.8 PPR points in any of those games. He has been largely out-snapped and out-produced by Rhamondre Stevenson, and we don't envision that trend changing on Sunday. Henderson's outlook would be murky even if he were fully healthy, but the ankle injury also complicates matters. He's currently listed as questionable, and while it seems like he's slightly leaning toward playing, that's far from guaranteed right now. If there's any saving grace, it's the fact that the Jets have allowed the ninth-most fantasy points and seventh-most rushing yards to running backs in 2026. Managers playing in deeper leagues or dealing with plenty of running back injuries may want to keep an eye on his injury status heading into Sunday, but otherwise, he's simply worth benching in most formats.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson Hoping to Play in Week 6
metadata.description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) said he is "hoping" he can play in his team's Week 6 matchup against the New York Jets, per ESPN's Mike Reiss. Henderson suffered an ankle injury during New England's Week 5 win over the Las Vegas Raiders that was initially expected to keep him out for multiple weeks, but he's officially listed as questionable to play against the Jets. Across four games so far in 2026, the 23-year-old has recorded 42 carries for 163 yards and a touchdown. If Henderson is active, it could heavily swing the fantasy outlook for fellow Patriots back Rhamondre Stevenson. Stevenson recorded 23 touches in Week 1, which Henderson missed due to injury. In the four games where he's shared the field with Henderson, Stevenson has yet to log more than 16 touches in a game.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) questionable for Sunday
metadata.description: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the New York Jets.
metadata.analysis: Henderson suffered a high-ankle sprain last week, but he may not have to miss any time because of it, as he is officially considered questionable to play in Week 6. Fantasy managers shouldn't trust starting him even if he's active, however, and Rhamondre Stevenson will be a quality starting option if the young running back is ruled out against the Jets.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson - Hopes to play Sunday
metadata.description: Henderson said Friday that an MRI revealed he sustained a high-ankle sprain but that he is "hoping to play" Sunday against the Jets, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
metadata.analysis: It was reported earlier in the week that Henderson was facing a multi-week absence due to a high-ankle sprain, and while he was indeed diagnosed with the more severe ankle issue, he was able to practice this week and will have a chance to take the field in Week 6.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) practicing Friday
metadata.description: TreVeyon Henderson was at practice again on Friday.
metadata.analysis: Henderson was limited in practice again on Thursday. It was seeming like he would be sidelined this week after suffering a high-ankle sprain, but he has practiced all week. He'll need to be monitored on the official injury report.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson - Practicing Friday
metadata.description: Henderson (ankle) is practicing Friday, Mark Daniels of MassLive.com reports.
metadata.analysis: After opening Week 6 prep with back-to-back limited sessions, Henderson is participating for a third straight day. Reports earlier this week suggested he would miss multiple games, but it now appears he has a chance to avoid any absences altogether. New England's final injury report will provide a better idea of where Henderson stands ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Jets.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson Questionable for Sunday Against Jets
metadata.description: New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said that running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's divisional clash against the New York Jets in Week 6, according to Mark Daniels of MassLive.com. This should be considered a best-case scenario for Henderson's fantasy managers after he was expected to miss multiple weeks following his ankle injury in the Week 5 win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. The 23-year-old was able to practice all week in a limited fashion, but instead of being out multiple weeks, he will have a chance to suit up on Sunday against the division-rival New York Jets. On the flip side, it will be hard to trust Henderson as a fantasy starter, even if he makes a remarkable turnaround to play this weekend. Henderson missed the season opener due to injury and has been the RB2 behind Rhamondre Stevenson, carrying the ball 42 times for 163 yards (3.9 yards per carry) and one touchdown while catching only two passes for 22 yards. Stevenson will have RB1 upside against Gang Green if Henderson is ruled out.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson Practicing Again on Friday
metadata.description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) was present again for the start of Friday's practice, according to team reporter Mark Daniels, capping off three straight days of practice after sustaining an ankle injury in the team's Week 5 win over the Raiders. Henderson was initially feared to be facing a multi-week absence, but after surprising with limited participation on Wednesday and Thursday, and showing up again on Friday, he has a chance to suit up for the team's divisional clash with the New York Jets on Sunday. Outside of one long run in a Week 2 win over the Steelers, Henderson has been inefficient in his second season, averaging 3.9 yards per carry and finding the end zone only once after scoring 10 times as a rookie. As such, even if active, he should be viewed as little more than a flex play despite a favorable matchup against the Jets.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) officially limited again Thursday
metadata.description: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) was officially limited at practice again on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Henderson was officially a limited participant at another practice on Thursday. He recently suffered a high-ankle sprain, but it's a very encouraging sign that it has not caused him to miss any practice time. It still seems more likely than not that he will be sidelined in Week 6, but we won't know for sure until after practice on Friday.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson - Limited again Thursday
metadata.description: Henderson (ankle) remained limited at Thursday's practice, Mark Daniels of MassLive reports.
metadata.analysis: Henderson has been limited in back-to-back practice sessions to kick off Week 6 prep. He'll likely need to upgrade to full participation Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into Sunday's home game against the Jets, in which second place in the AFC East will be on the line. Corey Kiner would be in line for change-of-pace work behind Rhamondre Stevenson if Henderson sits.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) practices Thursday
metadata.description: TreVeyon Henderson was seen practicing on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: It is noteworthy with Henderson dealing with a high-ankle sprain. He was also limited in practice on Wednesday. His status will need to be monitored in practice on Friday.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson - Set to practice in pads Thursday
metadata.description: Henderson (ankle) is in pads ahead of Thursday's practice, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
metadata.analysis: Henderson was a limited participant at Wednesday's practice, and he looks poised to practice in some capacity again Thursday, though the extent of his participation remains to bee seen. After initial pessimism following his exit from the Week 5 win over the Raiders, Henderson seemingly has a chance to suit up Sunday against the Jets without missing any additional game action.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson Present for Thursday's Practice
metadata.description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) was present for the team's practice on Thursday, according to Evan Lazar of the team's official website. Henderson was surprisingly listed as limited in the first practice of the week on Wednesday, and the Boston Herald's Doug Kyed reports that the 23-year-old was in pads before Thursday's session. After the second-year back was injured in the Week 5 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, it was expected that he would be headed for a multi-week absence. However, Henderson's ankle injury might not be as bad as initially feared, potentially giving him a chance to play this Sunday against the division-rival New York Jets in Week 6. The former Ohio State star will still be a risky RB3/flex option if he is active this weekend against the Jets, but it would be great news overall for his fantasy managers going forward. Henderson has not been able to get into a groove yet in 2026, averaging 3.9 yards per carry for 163 yards and one touchdown on 42 rushing attempts. He has added only two catches for 22 yards. If Henderson cannot play against New York, backfield mate Rhamondre Stevenson would be a must-start in fantasy lineups.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) logs limited practice Wednesday
metadata.description: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) logged a limited practice session on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Surprisingly, Henderson was able to practice in a limited fashion on Wednesday. He suffered a high-ankle sprain last week and was reported to be out multiple weeks because of it, but his participation indicates that it may not be as severe as the team initially anticipated. This is a situation fantasy managers should continue to monitor throughout the week.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson - Surprise practice participant Wednesday
metadata.description: The Patriots listed Henderson (ankle) as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
metadata.analysis: After Henderson was diagnosed with a right high-ankle sprain coming out of Sunday's win over the Raiders, Adam Schefter of ESPN reported Tuesday that the second-year running back would avoid surgery but was expected to miss multiple weeks. While that could still be the case, Henderson's involvement in practice Wednesday -- albeit in a limited capacity -- suggests that the Patriots haven't yet ruled him out from playing Week 6 against the Jets. However, in the more likely event that Henderson ends up sitting out this Sunday, Rhamondre Stevenson would be in store for a larger share of the touches out of the backfield, while Corey Kiner would serve as the top complement to Stevenson.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson - Absent for first Week 6 practice
metadata.description: Henderson (ankle) isn't participating in Wednesday's practice, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
metadata.analysis: Henderson's absence hardly comes as a surprise after Adam Schefter of ESPN reported that the running back is likely to miss multiple weeks after sustaining a right high-ankle sprain during this past Sunday's win over the Raiders. Head coach Mike Vrabel has yet to provide an updated timeline for Henderson's return, but the 23-year-old is expected to be officially ruled out for this Sunday's game against the Jets following Friday's practice.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) to miss multiple weeks
metadata.description: TreVeyon Henderson will miss multiple weeks due to a high-ankle sprain.
metadata.analysis: Henderson left Sunday's game early and was reevaluated Monday. On a positive note, the young running back will not require surgery, but he is going to miss some games. Veteran Rhamondre Stevenson will take over as the ball carrier in Henderson's absence.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson - Out multiple weeks with high-ankle sprain
metadata.description: Henderson is expected to miss multiple weeks after he was diagnosed with a right high-ankle sprain following an MRI on Monday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
metadata.analysis: Henderson sustained the injury in the second quarter of Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders and was unable to return. Schefter notes that Henderson won't need surgery to address the ankle sprain, so the running back may be able to avoid a stint on injured reserve and the automatic four-game absence that comes with it. Even so, Henderson still looks poised to be sidelined for at least a couple of contests, which will clear the way for Rhamondre Stevenson to take on a heightened role out of the backfield. Corey Kiner will also be in line for increased snaps as the top change-of-pace option behind Stevenson while Henderson is out of the mix.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson Suffers High-Ankle Sprain, Set to Miss Multiple Weeks
metadata.description: According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson is expected to miss multiple weeks due to a high ankle sprain. The running back exited their contest against the Las Vegas Raiders early and is now set to be on the sidelines for at least the next few weeks. Schefter noted that the second-year back is not expected to undergo surgery, and the Patriots hope he can return "sooner rather than later." It is worth noting that Henderson missed the season opener due to an ankle injury as well. This season, Henderson enjoyed one productive effort back in Week 2, where he ran for 76 yards and scored, but averaged a modest 4.0 PPR points in Weeks 3 and 4. While he remains out, Rhamondre Stevenson projects to see a massive workload and could push for mid-end RB2 upside.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) to be re-evaluated Monday
metadata.description: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said the team will re-evaluate RB TreVeyon Henderson on Monday.
metadata.analysis: Henderson left Sunday's game early against the Raiders with an ankle injury. His status will need to be monitored in practice throughout the week.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson - Headed for testing Monday
metadata.description: Henderson (ankle) is slated to undergo further medical testing Monday after exiting Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Henderson carried four times for 22 yards and recorded 16 receiving yards before exiting with just over 12 minutes left in the second quarter after injuring an ankle. Following Henderson's exit, Corey Kiner stepped in as the top complement to Rhamondre Stevenson, finishing the afternoon with six carries for 52 yards and a lost fumble. The Patriots didn't provide many details regarding the extent of Henderson's injury after the game, but the upcoming tests should shed more light on the matter. For now, Henderson can be considered questionable heading into the Patriots' Week 6 game against the Jets on Sunday.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson Undergoing an MRI Exam on Monday
metadata.description: New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said on Monday that running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) will have an MRI exam on Monday to determine if/how much time he will miss with an ankle injury that he suffered in the Week 5 win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, according to the NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe. Backfield mate Rhamondre Stevenson was questionable going into the game against the Raiders on Sunday due to a knee injury, but he managed to suit up and took over the backfield duties once Henderson was injured. The 23-year-old Henderson had a season-low four carries for 22 yards and caught his lone target for a gain of 16 yards before leaving with injury and not returning. Henderson also dealt with an ankle injury at the end of the preseason that caused him to sit out the Week 1 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. His status is worth watching closely this week. If Henderson cannot gain clearance to face the division-rival New York Jets in Week 6, Stevenson should handle the lion's share of backfield work for the Pats this weekend.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) ruled out
metadata.description: The Patriots have ruled out RB TreVeyon Henderson for the remainder of Week 5 with an ankle injury.
metadata.analysis: Henderson was injured in the first half and will not returning, leaving Rhamondre Stevenson as the primary running back. Henderson will finish the day with 22 rushing yards on four carries and one reception for 16 yards.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson - Makes early exit from Sunday's game
metadata.description: The Patriots ruled out Henderson (ankle) for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Raiders, Evan Lazar of the team's official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Initially considered questionable to return to the game after leaving in the second quarter due to the right ankle injury, Henderson didn't join the Patriots on the sideline to begin the second half before he was ruled out shortly after the third quarter got underway. He'll finish the afternoon with 22 yards on four carries to go with one catch for 16 yards. With Henderson sidelined for the rest of the contest, the Patriots will be left with Corey Kiner as their lone option behind No. 1 back Rhamondre Stevenson.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson (knee) questionable to return Sunday
metadata.description: TreVeyon Henderson (knee) is questionable to return for the New England Patriots against the Las Vegas Raiders Sunday according to Mike Reiss.
metadata.analysis: Henderson rushed four times for 22 yards while also catching his lone target for 16 yards prior to exiting. Rhamondre Stevenson should receive even more backfield work for head coach Mike Vrabel if Henderson is ruled out for the remainder of the Week 5 contest.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson - Suffers ankle injury in Week 5
metadata.description: Henderson suffered a right ankle injury during Sunday's game against the Raiders.
metadata.analysis: After a carry in the second quarter in which he endured an awkward tackle going out of bounds, Henderson limped to the locker room. The Patriots soon considered him questionable to return. Rhamondre Stevenson likely will take on the bulk of New England's backfield reps for as long as Henderson is sidelined, though Corey Kiner also is available for RB snaps.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson Ruled Out With Ankle Injury
metadata.description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's Week 5 game against the Las Vegas Raiders, according to Taylor Kyles. Henderson suffered the injury during the second quarter after being brought down along the sideline and headed to the locker room for further evaluation. He was initially questionable to return before being downgraded to out. The second-year back finished with four carries for 22 yards and one reception for 16 yards. He also gained 12 yards on a lateral before exiting.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson Questionable to Return With Ankle Injury
metadata.description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's Week 5 game against the Las Vegas Raiders due to an ankle injury. Mike Reiss of ESPN initially reported that Henderson headed to the locker room for further evaluation. He had three carries for 11 yards and caught his only target for four yards before leaving. The nature of the injury hasn't been announced. Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is active, with Corey Kiner also available in New England's backfield.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson Could Occupy Lead-Back Role in Week 5
metadata.description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson has been disappointing over the last two weeks, but he could get back onto the fantasy radar against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 5. Teammate Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is questionable to play, and if he can't suit up, Henderson could occupy the lead-back role. Presumably, if Stevenson doesn't play, Henderson would be in line to handle roughly 20 touches. That type of volume could lead to very favorable results, as the Raiders have allowed the sixth-most rushing yards to running backs entering this week. The 23-year-old hasn't scored a touchdown since Week 2, nor has he tallied more than 4.5 fantasy points in a game since then, so Sunday could be a get-right opportunity for the second-year back if he has the backfield all to himself. Managers interested in starting Henderson if Stevenson doesn't play should check back for an update when the Patriots post their list of inactive players on Sunday morning.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson - Could have expanded role vs. Las Vegas
metadata.description: Henderson would operate as the Patriots' RB1 if Rhamondre Stevenson (knee, questionable) is unable to play against the Raiders on Sunday, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Stevenson was limited in practice all week due to a knee injury, and while he expressed optimism on playing Friday, head coach Mike Vrabel was not quite ready to give the veteran running back the green light for Sunday's game, per Mark Daniels of MassLive.com. Stevenson's status for Week 5 will be worth a close watch, because if he's ruled out or is expected to operate under a snap count, then Henderson would be poised to take over as the Patriots' RB1 for at least one game. Henderson has a 38-141-1 rushing line through three games this season and has caught just one pass (on three targets) for six yards in that span.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson - Middling numbers in Week 4 win
metadata.description: Henderson rushed 14 times for 42 yards and failed to bring in either of his two targets in the Patriots' 29-26 win over the Bills on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Henderson struggled to get anything going against an improved Bills run defense, averaging an even 3.0 yards per carry. The second-year pro logged one more carry than backfield mate Rhamondre Stevenson but finished with five fewer rushing yards, and through three games, Henderson is averaging a pedestrian 3.7 yards per tote while only adding one catch for six yards. The 2025 second-round pick's next opportunity for his first breakout effort of 2026 comes in a Week 5 home matchup against a vastly improved Raiders team.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson sees 14 touches in Week 4 win
metadata.description: TreVeyon Henderson rushed for 42 yards on 14 carries in the Patriots win over the Bills. He did not record a reception on his two targets.
metadata.analysis: Henderson saw just one more carry that Rhamondre Stevenson, but failed to do much on his 14 touches. Fantasy managers should expect Stevenson and Henderson to continue to split time in the backfield in Week 5 against Las Vegas.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson in Prime Spot to Bounce Back
metadata.description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson came back down to earth with an extremely quiet showing last Sunday, but we're still trusting him as a mid-to-low RB2 option ahead of Week 4 against the Buffalo Bills. Henderson had just eight carries for 23 rushing yards (plus one reception) last Sunday. The low volume can be attributed to the fact that New England had nothing going on offense and had to throw the ball more, but that's still something to consider as fantasy managers set their lineup for Week 4. The good news is that, even though Buffalo is favored by seven points, the Bills' defense has been iffy and should give Henderson an opportunity to bounce back after last week's dud. So far, Buffalo's run defense has allowed the seventh-most fantasy points, 10th-most rushing touchdowns, third-most receptions, third-most receiving yards, and second-most receiving touchdowns to opposing running backs in 2026. Game script aside, this matchup presents an extremely encouraging fantasy outlook for Henderson. He ranks as RotoBaller's RB25 in Week 4, but there's no disputing his top-15 upside.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson Gives Back Ground in Patriots Backfield
metadata.description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson gave back some of the ground he gained in his season debut. Henderson handled 16 carries for 76 yards and a touchdown against Pittsburgh in Week 2, playing 60% of the offensive snaps. A week later in Jacksonville, that workload was cut in half. He finished with eight carries for 23 yards, caught one pass for six yards and was on the field for only 23 snaps, a 37% share. Rhamondre Stevenson played 33 snaps, and New England continued to rotate multiple backs in a game that got away from it early. Henderson still has the talent to make a smaller workload matter, but Week 3 was a reminder that he has not taken control of this backfield. After looking like the clear riser coming out of Week 2, his fantasy value has cooled with the Patriots heading to Buffalo in Week 4.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson totals 29 yards in loss Sunday
metadata.description: TreVeyon Henderson rushed the ball eight times for 23 yards and caught one pass for six yards in Sunday's 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: New England's offense wasn't able to get anything going on Sunday, and Henderson was no exception to that. He totaled just 29 yards on nine opportunities against the Jaguars, which burned any fantasy managers who started him in this matchup. He should not be started in most leagues until New England figures out their offensive issues.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson - Stymied in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: Henderson rushed eight times for 23 yards and brought in his only target for six yards in the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Playing in his second game of the season, Henderson led the Patriots in carries and rushing yards, but each of those figures were only one more than those generated by backfield mate Rhamondre Stevenson. Henderson had a much more efficient showing in his Week 2 season debut with a 16-carry, 76-yard, one-touchdown showing against the Steelers, but game script had a significant impact on the volume for both of the Patriots' backs Sunday. Henderson will look to get back on track in a key Week 4 road divisional matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson Held to 23 Yards Against Jaguars
metadata.description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson was quiet in Sunday's 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, finishing with eight carries for 23 yards. His longest run went for five yards, and New England never got much going on the ground. Rhamondre Stevenson had seven carries for 22 yards, while Corey Kiner added 18 yards on six attempts as the Patriots spread the work around. Henderson's line was a big step back from his 2026 debut against Pittsburgh, when he ran 16 times for 76 yards and a touchdown. New England was down 28-3 by the end of the third quarter, so the game got away from them quickly. Still, the drop from 16 carries to eight stands out. Henderson remains fantasy relevant, but Sunday's usage showed Stevenson and Kiner are still part of the backfield mix.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson Looks to Build Off Fantastic Season Debut
metadata.description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson had a very impressive performance in last week's season debut, and he'll look to replicate that success in another potentially favorable matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday afternoon. Henderson finished last weekend's game against the Steelers with 76 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown on 16 carries. Most notably, he reclaimed the lead-back role, relegating Rhamondre Stevenson to a much smaller role than expected. Assuming the backfield dynamic looks the same in Week 3, Henderson could be well on his way to a strong RB2 finish. The Jaguars have allowed the fourth-fewest rushing yards to running backs in 2026, but that's a small sample size that includes the Browns, who have struggled to get any sort of production from Quinshon Judkins, and the Broncos, who emerged from last week with all three of their running backs on the injury report. It's also worth noting that the Jaguars have still managed to surrender the seventh-most catches and receiving yards to running backs this year. Henderson ranks as the overall RB24 in RotoBaller's latest Week 3 fantasy football rankings.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson Emerges as the Primary Ball-Carrier in New England
metadata.description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson wasted no time solidifying himself in the lead-back role upon his return from injury. After Rhamondre Stevenson had 23 touches on an 85% snap share in Week 1, there was some speculation that he and Henderson would split the backfield snaps in Week 2. While they did have a relatively even 60/40 split in terms of snaps, Henderson out-touchded Stevenson 16 to 7. Additionally, Stevenson had a fumble while Henderson had a touchdown, further widening the gap between the two backs. Henderson finished his season debut with 16 carries, 76 rushing yards, and one touchdown, resulting in a solid 14.6-point outing in most fantasy leagues. Assuming he continues to handle the bulk of the volume out of the backfield, the 23-year-old will be a high-end RB2 with RB1 upside going forward.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson finds the end zone in season debut
metadata.description: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson tallied 76 rushing yards and a touchdown on 16 carries in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers.
metadata.analysis: Henderson missed Week 1 with an ankle injury, but made an immediate impact with a 39-yard touchdown early in the win over Pittsburgh. Rhamondre Stevenson lost a fumble and saw the bulk of the work go to Henderson after the turnover. Fantasy managers should expect both Stevenson and Henderson to have roles against the Jaguars in Week 3.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson - Scores 39-yard TD in season debut
metadata.description: Henderson (ankle) rushed 16 times for 76 yards and a touchdown and wasn't targeted in the passing game during Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers.
metadata.analysis: Henderson didn't take long to make an impact in his season debut after sitting out the 13-10 Week 1 loss to Seattle. The 2025 second-round pick opened the scoring with a 39-yard touchdown run 6:38 into Sunday's game and handled 17 touches compared to just seven for Rhamondre Stevenson, who lost a fumble on the drive preceding Henderson's touchdown run. Henderson had 180 carries to Stevenson's 130 during the 2025 regular season. Both running backs are likely to be involved in the Week 3 game plan against the Jaguars.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson Scores TD in Solid Week 2 Effort
metadata.description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson contributed to his team's blowout win against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 2, rushing for 76 yards on 16 carries and scoring a touchdown. The 23-year-old Ohio State product outplayed the Patriots' de facto RB1 Rhamondre Stevenson, who had six carries for 43 yards on Sunday. Henderson, who missed Week 1 with an ankle injury, had 180 carries for 911 yards and nine touchdowns over 17 regular season games his rookie season for the Patriots, adding 35 receptions for 221 yards and one touchdown in the air over that span. RotoBaller lists Henderson at RB41 in the position rankings, and his fantasy stock should go up if he continues to produce at this level.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson Likely Splitting the Workload in His Return
metadata.description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson will make his season debut on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Henderson missed Week 1 due to an ankle injury, but his absence was short-lived, as he has been cleared to return in Week 2 against the Pittsburgh Steelers. At this point, we expect Henderson to share snaps with Rhamondre Stevenson, who drew the start in the season opener. Stevenson had 23 touches last week, and he played a major role in the receiving game. We wouldn't be shocked to see both Henderson and Stevenson log at least 10-15 touches this Sunday, especially with wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) no longer involved on offense after he was placed on injured reserve. Henderson has jumped to RB41 in RotoBaller's latest fantasy football rankings, but managers would be justified starting him as an RB3/flex in Week 2.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson Officially Cleared for Week 2
metadata.description: New England Patriots second-year running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) practiced in full all week and was not on the team's final injury report on Friday, clearing the way for him to make his season debut on Sunday in a Week 2 matchup against the visiting Pittsburgh Steelers, per the team's official website. The 23-year-old former Ohio State star RB was held out of the Week 1 season-opening loss last Wednesday to the Seattle Seahawks due to an ankle injury that he suffered late in training camp. He has made great progress this week, though, and is ready to rejoin a backfield that also includes Rhamondre Stevenson. The Patriots' coaching staff still has plenty of trust in Stevenson, but he averaged a paltry 2.8 yards per carry last week, and they will surely welcome Henderson and his explosive backfield abilities back into the fold. In what should be a near-even timeshare between Stevenson and Henderson, Henderson should not be much more than an RB3/flex option for fantasy managers in his 2026 debut.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) officially good to go for Sunday
metadata.description: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is off of the injury report and officially good to go for Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
metadata.analysis: New England's offense is set to get a much-needed boost this week with their young running back off of the injury report and set to make his season debut on Sunday. Henderson projects to be something of a 'boom-or-bust' fantasy option on a week-to-week basis while he continues to split work with Rhamondre Stevenson in the Patriots' backfield.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) ready for season debut
metadata.description: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) has been practicing in full this week and will be ready for Sunday's game.
metadata.analysis: Henderson was unable to go in Week 1, leaving the bulk of the backfield load to veteran Rhamondre Stevenson. Henderson is in his second NFL season after totaling over 1,100 yards of offense and 10 touchdowns across 17 regular-season games as a rookie.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) logs full practice Thursday
metadata.description: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) logged a full practice session on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Henderson was able to log a second-straight full practice session on Thursday. He seems almost certain to play without any real limitations this week, as he also told reporters that he is ready to go for Sunday's game. His return to the lineup will mean less work for Rhamondre Stenson moving forward, but they could both be worthwhile starters on any given week.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) 'ready to go' for Week 2
metadata.description: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) told reporters that he is "ready to go" ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
metadata.analysis: It looks like Henderson is finally healthy after missing the season opener due to an ankle injury. He was able to log a full practice on Wednesday and told reporters that he is "ready to go" on Thursday, which puts him squarely on track to play this week. His likely presence will mean less work for Rhamondre Stevenson moving forward, though it will benefit the offense as a whole.

metadata.title: TreVeyon Henderson - Says he's ready to go
metadata.description: Henderson (ankle) said Thursday that he's ready to go for Sunday's game against the Steelers, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Henderson sat out the Patriots' Week 1 loss to the Seahawks but has been practicing without limitations ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Steelers. Rhamondre Stevenson handled 23 touches in Henderson's absence last week, but they figure to shift into a near-even split, leaving few, if any, touches for third-stringer Corey Kiner.
